bear_case: The DXY at 99.57 — not the estimated 97.80 in the prior brief — is the morning's defining correction: the Iran deal only pushed the dollar approximately 0.5 points below 100, not the 2.2 points the June 16 morning brief assumed, and at 0.43 from the trigger a single hawkish sentence from Warsh could simultaneously breach both the DXY and 30Y regime thresholds before the close. May CPI at 4.2% leaves the dot plot with no statistical justification for 2026 cut projections; if three or more FOMC members submit hike dots and Warsh's language signals a tightening bias, equities at 22.7x forward P/E face a 4–7% multiple compression that oil disinflation alone cannot offset. The VIX futures term structure — spot 16.42 versus the June futures contract at 18.28 — is the market pricing in exactly this scenario, and a spot VIX close above 18 post-Warsh would simultaneously breach the NVDA add trigger. If SPX closes below 7,460 following the Warsh June 17 presser, BUY reverts to HOLD immediately — do not wait for a second session.
